statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail stays in the low band after a cash session that fully retraced its gap and closed flat, while Stress rises with explicit October rate-hike repricing and a 33-year-high seven-year auction yield.
recommendation: Thursday's Nasdaq-100 session opened roughly 0.8% below the prior close, based at 30,204.16, retraced the entire gap to 30,529.35 and settled at 30,478.86, up 0.03%. Mean reversion functioned in both directions across the full range and VIX decayed from a 16.57 high to 15.67, so the observed price path is the opposite of the pathological structure the Tail score measures. Stress is raised to 57 because markets now price roughly a 64% probability of an October rate hike and over 48% for December, the seven-year auction cleared at a 33-year-high yield with weaker indirect demand, and Brent above $107 leaves the Strait of Hormuz standoff unresolved. Equity futures reopened at 21:00Z and no evening price path is observable yet. The narrow danger window covers Friday's 12:30Z Durable Goods release and the 13:30Z US cash open. Tail remains below the block threshold.
headline: Nasdaq-100 fully retraces its gap to close flat at 30,478.86; Tail stays low while Stress rises on explicit October rate-hike repricing
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed at 30,478.86, up 8.56 points or 0.03%, against a 30,470.29 prior close. It opened at 30,225.19, about 0.8% below that close, based at 30,204.16, then recovered the whole gap to a 30,529.35 high and settled in the upper half of a 325-point range, roughly 1.07%. December NQ futures settled at 30,736.25, down 0.09%, inside a 30,370.00 to 30,827.50 range. Both sides of that range were traded with completed retracements, which is the central reason Tail remains in the low band: the risk contract defines Tail as the probability that mean reversion fails long enough to create a persistent one-way path, and a full gap retrace with a flat close is direct evidence against that structure. VIX closed at 15.67, up 3.23%, but well off its 16.57 session high and only modestly above a 15.34 low, so the volatility impulse decayed rather than extended. The stress backdrop is nonetheless harder than it was at the previous publication. The clearest new evidence is explicit policy repricing: markets are now discounting roughly a 64% probability of a further 25 basis point rate increase in October and more than 48% for December. That is a tightening path rather than the easing path equities were positioned for, and it is being expressed through term premium at the long end. The Treasury sold close to $44bn of seven-year notes at a 5.085% high yield, the highest since April 1993, tailing a 5.078% market yield, with bid-to-cover at 2.42 against 2.50 last month and indirect bidders at 57.2% against roughly 61%. The 10-year traded near 5.16% with a 5.09% to 5.18% range, its highest since 2007, and the 30-year reached about 5.43%, its highest since 2004; some venues quote the 10-year above 5.2%, so the exact print is dispersed across sources. The H.15 release for 23 September carried the 2-year at 4.85%, the 10-year at 5.11% and the 30-year at 5.40%. Energy remains the second pressure source. WTI is near $94.76, up 2.82% after peaking around $97, and Brent near $107.03, up 3.83%, leaving Brent up more than 17% in September. Prices came off their highs on a Reuters report that US and Iranian negotiators are exploring a phased agreement under which Iran would permit transit through the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for Washington ending its economic blockade. That negotiation is genuinely two-sided and unresolved, which is why it informs Stress and the danger-window placement rather than the current Tail score. Index internals were dispersed rather than aligned: Meta gained about 4.5% and Alphabet 1.34%, while Arm fell 7.88%, Qualcomm 1.51% and Broadcom 1.3%, with semiconductor dispersion near 3.5 percentage points. Oracle fell after reporting a force majeure notice on a New Mexico data-centre project. Dispersion of that kind reduces directional conviction and supports the mixed dominant mode rather than raising Tail. Under the risk contract a weak auction, a hawkish rate repricing, an energy shock and high-importance headlines raise Stress and inform Confidence; they do not establish Tail on their own. Tail would require observed persistent directional efficiency, shallow or failed retracements and a hold near session extremes, none of which occurred. Confidence is set at 86 rather than higher because CME equity futures reopened at 21:00Z after the 20:00Z to 21:00Z halt and both futures feeds still print pre-halt values at the assessment cutoff, so the current hour carries verified levels but no observable evening price path. Shared Finviz context was about 37 minutes old and partial, with its futures and calendar sections unavailable, so it was used only as latest-session breadth, megacap and semiconductor context and for headline discovery, and every current level was taken from primary sources.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 published hours held a watch-band regime with a single orange print. Tail ran 20-21 through Wednesday's late US session, eased to 17-19 across the Asian overnight, then rebuilt through a trend-down European morning to a 25 peak at 09:00Z, the only BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES slot in the window. Across Thursday's US session Tail oscillated between 19 and 24 without establishing persistent one-way structure, and the final three published hours settled at 21, 20 and 19 as the cash session completed its gap retrace. Stress climbed steadily from 51-54 overnight to 56-57 by the close as long-end yields and crude both extended. Confidence stayed in the 85-88 band throughout.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours run from a thin futures reopen through the Asian and European sessions into Friday's US cash session. Conditional Tail stays in the low-to-watch band and never reaches a blocking level, because raising it further would require observed persistent structure that does not exist at the assessment cutoff. It eases to 18 across the quiet late-evening hours, builds to 22-23 through the European morning where the lookback's only orange print occurred, and peaks at 24 across the 12:00Z Durable Goods release and the 13:30Z US cash open. Stress peaks at 62 in the cash-open hour and stays elevated all session on record long-end yields, October hike pricing and an unresolved Gulf negotiation. The final slot returns to the low band because it covers the 20:00Z to 21:00Z futures halt, in which no tradable price path exists.
